blocks.content: The State shall take steps to organize village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.

items: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) originally recommended the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system.
Rajasthan was the first state in independent India to establish Panchayati Raj, inaugurated in Nagaur district on October 2, 1959.
Article 243D mandates reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Women.
Elections to Panchayati Raj Institutions are conducted independently by the State Election Commission under Article 243K.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Panchayati Raj System was constitutionalized through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
The three-tier structure comprises Gram Panchayat at the village level, Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and Zilla Parishad at the district level.
Part IX was added to the Constitution of India, titled 'The Panchayats', covering Articles 243 to 243O.
The 11th Schedule explicitly lists 29 functional matters devolved to the Panchayati Raj Institutions.
Mandatory reservation of not less than one-third (33%) of total seats is provided for women across all tiers.
